Here is a concise but comprehensive summary of what I know about Erik Ninn‑Hansen.

Basic identity and political alignment
- Erik Ninn‑Hansen was a senior Danish politician, affiliated with the Conservative People’s Party (Det Konservative Folkeparti). He was a prominent figure in Danish national politics from the 1960s through the 1980s.

Political career and positions
- He held several high-level posts in government and in the Folketing (the Danish Parliament), including ministerial positions in Conservative-led or coalition governments and senior parliamentary roles. He served in the cabinets of the period that included Prime Minister Poul Schlüter.
- During his ministerial career he had responsibility for interior/immigration matters and for justice at different times (he was one of the leading figures in policy areas that included asylum, family reunification and immigration controls).

The Tamil Case (Tamil‑sagen)
- Erik Ninn‑Hansen is best known internationally and historically for his central role in the so‑called “Tamil Case,” a political/administrative scandal in Denmark in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
- The core of the case: as a minister he instructed administrative authorities to stop or delay processing of family‑reunification applications from Tamil refugees from Sri Lanka, in part by ordering files to be placed “on the top shelf” or otherwise withheld from routine processing. Those actions were done to limit the number of refugees/family members allowed into Denmark.
- The actions were found to be illegal and in breach of ministerial duties and administrative law because they involved unlawful interference with civil servants’ handling of individual cases and denial of rights to applicants.
- The scandal produced a major parliamentary inquiry and widespread public debate in Denmark about ministerial responsibility, the rule of law, and treatment of refugees.

Impeachment, conviction and consequences
- The parliamentary inquiry and its aftermath led to formal proceedings. Erik Ninn‑Hansen was impeached (brought before the Court of Impeachment of the Realm — Rigsretten), found criminally culpable for abuse of power related to the Tamil Case, and was convicted. He received a penal sanction (a suspended prison sentence).
- The case was politically and constitutionally significant in Denmark: it underscored the principle that ministers can be held personally and criminally accountable for unlawful orders and misuse of administrative power. It damaged the reputation and political standing of Ninn‑Hansen personally and had broader political repercussions for his party and the government coalition of the time.

Legacy and significance
- Ninn‑Hansen’s name is strongly associated in Denmark with the Tamil Case and with debates about ministerial accountability, immigration policy, and the boundaries between political direction and unlawful interference in individual administrative decisions.
- The scandal triggered reflection and some reforms in administrative practice and strengthened public awareness about legal protections for asylum seekers and family‑reunification applicants.

Notes and caveats
- I have summarized the widely known facts and the major consequences of Ninn‑Hansen’s career. If you want precise chronology (exact dates of birth/death, the exact offices and dates he held them, the year(s) of the inquiry, the exact sentence imposed, or full quotes from the inquiry or Rigsretten judgment), I can look up and provide those specific details.
